clue.text: This regularly thrashes giants

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the word This, starting with the first, gives a regular pick

parts.note: tans, as in 'tan someone's hide', means thrashes

explanation.surface: A boast that something routinely beats far bigger opponents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 1st and 3rd letters of 'This', giving TI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were the race of giant gods of Greek myth, so the word is used for any giant.

clue.text: After tax rises American banking centre showing resolve

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: pay after tax is net pay
the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: Someone staying firm as taxes climb in an American financial hub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After tax' looks like a time phrase but means net pay, which 'rises' turns upward; 'showing' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolve as a noun is firmness of purpose, a synonym for doggedness and persistence.

clue.text: Number teeming around European island

indicators.note: the two words ten and rife sit around the European letter, enclosing it between them

parts.note: ten is a number
rife means teeming, abundant

explanation.surface: A crowded European holiday island packed with visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' has the number and the teeming word sit either side of the European letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenerife is the largest of the Canary Islands, a Spanish island off West Africa.

clue.text: Earns ridiculous advances

indicators.note: something ridiculous is absurd or out of order, so the letters of the word are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is paid absurdly large advances on their earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earns' looks like the definition and 'advances' like money paid up front; really 'advances' is a verb meaning approaches.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance towards something is to draw closer to it, approach it.

clue.text: Ravage partner after start of month

indicators.note: the partner word comes after the start of the month in the answer

parts.note: Dec I, the first of December, is the start of a month
a mate is a partner

explanation.surface: Someone attacking their partner as the month begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of month' is a date, DEC I (1 December), not the letter M.
explanation.definitionFit: To ravage is to devastate or destroy a large part of something, the modern sense of the word.

clue.text: Cover-up at a high level?

parts.note: a political scandal hushed up by the top brass, but also the Moon covering up the Sun high in the sky

explanation.surface: A question about a cover-up among senior officials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover-up' suggests a scandal; read literally, it is one body hiding another, high up in the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: In an eclipse one heavenly body covers another, high in the sky.

clue.text: Opening of clumsy packaging caught one performing

indicators.note: the word for clumsy wraps the letter for caught, packaging it

parts.note: inept means clumsy
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
I is the Roman numeral one
a performer on stage is on

explanation.surface: A clumsy package is opened, catching someone on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packaging' puts C inside INEPT to give INCEPT.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening means a beginning or start, the moment something is founded.

clue.text: Heads of armed police outlaw ladies licentiously ogling handsome youth

indicators.note: the heads of the six words are their first letters

parts.words: armed police outlaw ladies licentiously ogling

explanation.surface: A lurid tabloid scene: armed police banning women who leer at a pretty young man.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollo, the Greek god, is the classic image of male beauty, so any handsome young man may be called one.

clue.text: English judge lacking proper authority

indicators.note: the judge word goes without the letter for proper, lacking it

parts.note: an umpire judges a game
U means upper-class, so proper or socially acceptable

explanation.surface: An English judge said to be without proper authority.
explanation.walkthrough: U as 'upper-class, proper' is a British convention (U and non-U).
explanation.definitionFit: An empire is a sphere of authority or control, as in a business empire.

clue.text: Crab maybe unable to move

indicators.note: letters set to move are shifted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A crab that cannot get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crab' suggests the crustacean, but it is the Crab Nebula in Taurus.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crab Nebula is a well-known example of a glowing interstellar cloud of gas and dust.

clue.text: About to cut into love without compare

indicators.note: the about and cut words go into the word for love

parts.note: nil, zero, is love in tennis scoring
on means about, concerning
to pare is to cut or trim

explanation.surface: Some tender love so special it has no equal, about to be cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as one phrase meaning imminent; it must be split into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing without compare is unrivalled, matchless, which this borrowed French word means.

clue.text: Disorder in court following short cut

indicators.note: the court word comes after the cut word
the cut word made short loses its final letter

parts.note: to crop is to cut
someone up before the judge is in court

explanation.surface: A disturbance in court after a short trim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in court' is as in being up before the magistrates.
explanation.definitionFit: Croup is a childhood throat ailment with a barking cough, a medical disorder.

clue.text: Carries constant gifts

parts.note: c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
arts are skills or talents, gifts

explanation.surface: Someone who always brings presents.
explanation.definitionFit: To cart something is to carry or lug it, usually something bulky.

clue.text: Happy about entering Arctic perhaps after peacekeeping force gets out

indicators.note: the polar piece comes after the peacekeepers' letters

parts.note: the UN, United Nations, sends peacekeeping forces

indicators.note: the reversed happy word goes inside the polar word

parts.note: the Arctic is one polar region

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word for happy is read backwards

parts.note: up means cheerful, as in feeling up

explanation.surface: Cheerful UN peacekeepers heading into the Arctic, and then leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns UP to PU, which 'entering' puts in POLAR; 'gets' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Out, as in out of favour, means disliked or no longer liked by the public.

clue.text: Material round round cheese

indicators.note: the first round tells us to turn the next word around

parts.note: round means plump or rotund, so fat
feta is a Greek cheese

explanation.surface: Fabric wrapped around a round cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'round' is the reversal signal acting on the second, which means plump.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp, lustrous fabric of silk or similar, used for dresses.

clue.text: Try charm to overwhelm very old unionist

indicators.note: the charm word surrounds the other letters, engulfing them

parts.note: to endear is to make liked, to charm
U stands for Unionist, as in the Ulster Unionists of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Using charm to win over an old Unionist politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to overwhelm' puts VOU inside ENDEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A try is an attempt or effort, a synonym for the noun.

clue.text: Pantomime villain's secret vice

indicators.note: something secret is concealed, so the answer lies concealed across the words Pantomime villain

explanation.surface: Gossip about what a panto baddie gets up to off stage.
explanation.walkthrough: A pantomime is a British Christmas stage show whose villain is hissed by the audience. The answer runs across the end of 'Pantomime' and the start of 'villain'.
explanation.definitionFit: Vice as a noun is wickedness or immoral conduct, a synonym for sin.

clue.text: Split personality's seedy raincoat

definitions.note: a personality from Split, a city on the Adriatic; the 's stands for 'is'

indicators.note: seedy means shabby and run-down, so the letters are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: Someone with a split personality wearing a shabby raincoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split personality' suggests a psychiatric condition; Split is a city on the Dalmatian coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the Adriatic port of Split is a native of that Balkan country.

clue.text: Added appropriate punctuation to pop up advertisement involving female on date

indicators.note: in a down clue the date letter sits on, below, the rest
the advertising word takes in the female bird, involving it

parts.note: hype is aggressive promotion that pumps up a product
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: A pop-up ad featuring a woman on a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop up' reads like an internet ad but means to puff up; 'involving' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Joining words with a short dash, as in pop-up, is the punctuation the definition describes.

clue.text: Likelihood of excessive drug intake by police officer

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces are placed side by side

parts.note: OD is an overdose
DS is a detective sergeant

explanation.surface: How likely an overdose is near a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: The odds of something are the chances or probability that it will happen.

clue.text: Turning point in short car journey led all over the place

parts.note: a spin is a short drive for pleasure

indicators.note: letters all over the place are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A quick drive that led to a decisive moment and chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning point' suggests a crisis; read literally, it is a rod on which things turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A spindle is a rod or pin on which something rotates, literally a point of turning.

clue.text: Offender pronounced extremely guilty offers co-operation

indicators.note: the clue word is given as spoken, not as written

parts.note: a sinner is an offender against moral law

indicators.note: the extremes of guilty are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An offender declared guilty agrees to work with the authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: SINNER said out loud gives SYNER; the ends of 'guilty' add GY; 'offers' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Synergy is combined working in which the whole achieves more than the parts, joint action.

clue.text: Comic scene featuring soprano on boat

indicators.note: in a down clue, the soprano letter sits on, above, the boat

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A comic scene with a singer aboard a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a short humorous performance, a scene in a revue or comedy show.

clue.text: Spun endlessly to unroll

indicators.note: without its ends, the word for spun loses its first and last letters

parts.note: revolved means spun round

explanation.surface: Something spinning on and on until it unwinds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' strips the R and D off REVOLVED.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin root means to roll out, and the word once meant to unfold or unwind.

clue.text: Decreased desultory derision is misplaced

indicators.note: desultory means random and haphazard, so the letters are scattered into a new order
the word is is missing, mislaid, from the letters of derision

explanation.surface: Scorn shown half-heartedly loses its place and dwindles.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove IS from the letters of DERISION, then rearrange what is left. 'Decreased' looks like 'reduced' but means 'de-creased', with the creases taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing cloth smooth with a hot iron takes the creases out of it.

clue.text: Resourceful relatives adapted

indicators.note: adapted means altered, so the letters are changed into another arrangement

explanation.surface: Relatives who adjusted cleverly to a change.
explanation.definitionFit: Being resourceful means being adaptable and able to turn your hand to many things.

clue.text: Area used to be hot and covered in water

parts.note: was means used to be
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A region that was once hot but is now flooded.
explanation.definitionFit: Awash means flooded, swamped by the sea or rain.

clue.text: A as in Athens

parts.note: the first letter as a Greek in Athens would name it, the counterpart of the Roman A

explanation.surface: A spelling-alphabet phrase: A as in Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a phonetic spelling code; it asks for the Greek name of the letter A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek alphabet begins with this letter, which corresponds to the Roman A.

clue.text: Popular attempt to follow Latin argot

indicators.note: the popular and attempt words come after, follow, the Latin letter

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: A trendy effort at Latin slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Argot is the jargon or private vocabulary of a group, which is what this slang word means.

clue.text: Unfortunate, poetic end to story

indicators.note: an unfortunate arrangement of these letters is a bad one, so they are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A literary critic laments a tale's sadly poetic ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'story' looks like a narrative, but here a story is a lie; 'to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A story, as in telling stories, is a lie, a piece of trickery.

clue.text: Got behind in final round getting bothered without leader

parts.note: the end is the final part
O is round in shape

indicators.note: the bothered word loses its first letter, its leader

parts.note: arsed is British slang for bothered, as in can't be arsed

explanation.surface: Someone getting upset in the final round of a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: ARSED is British slang: 'can't be arsed' means can't be bothered.
explanation.definitionFit: To get behind a cause or candidate is to back, support or approve it.

clue.text: Is able to study when head-over-heels drunk

parts.note: can means is able to

indicators.note: head over heels means upside down, so the study word is turned back to front

parts.note: a den is a private study

explanation.surface: Someone who can only study while falling-down drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head-over-heels' reverses DEN to NED.
explanation.definitionFit: Canned is slang for intoxicated, tanked up with drink.
